The hidden setup gives you `quotes`: the first 20 Fluvia quote lines, one dict per line.

## Exercise: net value of a quote line

Compute the net value in EUR of the first quote line `quotes[0]` and store it in `net_value`.

```{pyodide}
#| exercise: net_value
q = quotes[0]
net_value = ______
net_value
```

```{pyodide}
#| exercise: net_value
#| setup: true
{{< include setup.py >}}
```

```{pyodide}
#| exercise: net_value
#| check: true
{{< include ../../components/check.py >}}
```

::: {.hint exercise="net_value"}
Start with the gross value: how many pieces, at what price each?
:::

::: {.hint exercise="net_value"}
The discount is stored in percent. Turn it into a factor first.
:::

::: {.hint exercise="net_value"}
A discount of 3 % leaves 97 % of the gross value: `1 - discount_pct / 100`.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="net_value"}
```python
q = quotes[0]
net_value = q["quantity"] * q["unit_price_eur"] * (1 - q["discount_pct"] / 100)
```
:::

## Quote values as a chart

```{pyodide}
#| autorun: true
#| caption: Chart
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import csv

with open("data/quotes.csv", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f, delimiter=";"))[:20]
values = [int(r["quantity"]) * float(r["unit_price_eur"].replace(",", ".")) for r in rows]
plt.bar([r["quote_id"][-3:] for r in rows], values)
plt.ylabel("Gross value (EUR)")
plt.title("First 20 Fluvia quote lines")
plt.show()
```
